OUR MISSION 


“The Montreal YMCA is a partnership of 
volunteers and staff committed to the 
fulfillment of people in spirit, mind and 
body, and to the development of self- 
reliance in the individual and _ the 
community. 


Through its actions, programs and 
services, the Montreal YMCA will reflect 
the needs and aspirations of the 
communities and will work with 
individuals, local communities and 
communities in developing countries in 
achieving social justice and control of 
their environments.” 


\”/

MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD AND THE PRESIDENT 
AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER OF THE MONTREAL YMCA 


On behalf of the staff and volunteers, we are pleased to report on the 
highlights of the Montreal YMCA’s 144th year of service to the Greater 
Montreal community. The year was marked with the on-going challenge of 
meeting the growing needs of the less fortunate in our society and, at the 
same time, ensuring the Association’s long-term financial viability. We take 
comfort in the knowledge that we continued to make progress on both these 
fronts. 


We are particularly proud of our accomplishments in serving the youth of our 
community. Of the 75,000 people in the Greater Montreal area who participate 
in YMCA programs, over 50% are under 18 years of age. The services we offer 
range from day-care to camping, from pre and after-school care to fitness 
and skill classes and from baby-sitting to counseling teens who have 
committed misdemeanors. 


In the past year, we added drop-in centers at Pointe-Saint-Charles, Centre- 
ville, Kirkland, Baie D’Urfe and Westmount to those already in existence at 
Douglas-Shand, Du Parc and NDG. We welcome young people under the age of 
18 at these facilities at no cost. In addition to the companionship of their 
peers in a safe environment, these teenagers benefit from a number of 
programs specifically designed for them by our skilled and dedicated youth 
workers. There are over 500 young people who drop in our centers every day. 
They are offered tutoring, counseling, as well as recreational and educational 
programming. 


One of our major initiatives in the past year was to make a significant 
investment to upgrade our fitness equipment and facilities. We also 
participated in a nationwide initiative called « Priority SAM », the goal of 
which is to improve the quality of service to YMCA members. The investment 
has already had positive results. The number of members is up and member 
satisfaction, as measured in a survey conducted in June 1996, improved 
considerably over the previous year. 


Another major step forward was the installation of a management 
information system. This long-overdue initiative will enable us to become 
increasingly efficient and to offer better quality services and programs by 
providing us with more accurate and timely data. The introduction has not 
been without some frustration as we continue to adapt and learn to work with 
this new technology. However, the response has been enthusiastic and the 
benefits of having the system are already evident. 


We completed our 3-year Strategic Plan, the focus of which is to continue our 
efforts to ensure the Montreal YMCA’s long-term financial viability. The 
measurable action plans are intended to (a) improve the efficiency of our 
existing operations, (b) redress the debt on the balance sheet, (c) create a 
significant new source of sustainable revenue and (d) become more effective 
in fund raising. By accomplishing these goals, the Montreal YMCA will be in a 
better position to meet the increasing need for financial subsidies and will 
have additional resources to fund development work in our community. 


In March 1996, the Enterprise Centre was made an independent entity from 
the Montreal YMCA. The Enterprise Centre was created in 1984 and, in the 
ensuing years, hundreds of new businesses were founded with the Enterprise 
Centre providing the training and the facilities to help launch young 
entrepreneurs. During the past 2 years, it has been difficult to finance the 
Centre without government assistance. To remain viable, the Centre has had 
to change its mission to one which is more directed towards consulting. To 
facilitate this change and to provide the Centre with the flexibility it required 
to solicit its own funding, the Montreal YMCA transferred the assets and the 
employees to a new not-for-profit corporation now operating under the name 
of The Montreal Enterprise Center. We wish the staff and volunteers of the 
Montreal Enterprise Center continued success. 


An exciting new initiative called Operation Espoir was launched during the 
year. In partnership with the noted Quebec film producer, Jean-Claude Lord, 
the government of the Province of Quebec, Videotron and the Montreal Urban 
Community Police Department, the YMCA collaborated in the design of the 
program and manages its activities. 


The objective of Operation Espoir is to create awareness and celebrate the 
benefits of the multi-cultural nature of Montreal society. The program entails 
the creation of small teams which include a mix of recent immigrants, young 
Canadians and a representative of the Police Department. Each team 
proposes and undertakes a project to highlight the richness of the 
community's cultural diversity and the most successful projects are 
publicized over local television. 


On the international front, the Montreal YMCA continued its work with and 
support of four YMCAs in Central and South America. One project of 
particular significance was the Partners for Children project. In 
collaboration with the Bancroft School and the YMCA of Ecuador, the Montreal 
YMCA published a book entitled "Hands Up” which is a training manual 
designed for people who work with children and youth. Its purpose is to 
foster a better understanding of childrens’ rights. There were a number of 
training sessions held with school board officials, YMCA personnel and 
interested people from other organizations. The response has been 
enthusiastic and the project has been heralded as an important step forward 
in the fight against the exploitation of children. 


The financial results for the year ended May 31, 1996 are presented in the 
Audited Statements which follow. Our financial statements are more 
complicated to understand this year because of a change which was imposed 
by the accounting profession on all not-for-profit organizations. In the past 
we accounted for our revenues on a cash basis. Beginning in the year just 
ended, we now account for our revenues on an accrual basis. In other words, 
rather than accounting as revenue a membership fee in total in the month it 
is paid, we now include only that portion which is earned in a given month. 


The net result of this change for the year ended May 31, 1996 is twofold. 
Firstly, the change in accounting method resulted in an impact of 
approximately $780,000 on the statement of revenues and expenses which 
caused a deficit of $701,661 for the year just ended. Secondly, because we 
were not able to reconstruct the statements for the year ended May 31, 1995 
from the cash to the accrual method of accounting, comparisons between the 
two fiscal years are not possible. We were however, satisfied with the 
financial results for the year ended May 31, 1996. 


They demonstrate that we continue on a positive trend in terms of increased 
revenues from continuing operations and higher levels of operating 
efficiency. 


The programs and services offered by the Montreal YMCA are more relevant 
today than at any time in its long history. People from all segments of our 
society are impacted by anxiety due to uncertainty. For many, job security is 
a thing of the past. Unemployment is high and young people, in particular, 
question what the future holds for them. Governments are attempting to 
resolve deficits by cutting back or eliminating certain social entitlement 
programs. Seniors are concerned about the quality and availability of health 
care. 


The Montreal YMCA strives to restore and promote self-confidence by offering 
programs and services designed to build strong individuals in Mind, Body and 
Spirit. Our mission, rooted in the underlying values of Respect, Honesty, 
Caring and Responsibility, is to empower individuals to take charge of their 
lives and meet the challenges of a rapidly changing environment. 


The Montreal YMCA is about people, those we serve, those who serve and 
those who help us serve. Those who serve are the staff and volunteers, 
without whose dedication and tireless effort, nothing would be accomplished. 
Those who help us serve are the individuals and organizations who contribute 
financially and provide us with the tools and the encouragement required to 
forge ahead. To all, we express our sincere appreciation for continuing to 
make the Montreal YMCA one of the most important and relevant social 
organizations in this community. 


CAN Leuublinatt 


Michael Novak Bernard W. Matte 
Chairman of the Board President & Chief Executive Officer 


BRANCH HIGHLIGHTS 


Centre-Ville YMCA 


There was a considerable improvement in year to year member satisfaction 
following a $200,000 investment on renovations and fitness equipment. The 
Youth Drop-In Centre was opened in April and the response has been very 
positive. 


The Residence/Cafeteria had another excellent year. The program of 
refurbishment assisted greatly in attracting new clients. The first ever 
conference for francophone professionals in the field of fitness and aerobics 
was held in February. 


Douglas-Shand YMCA 


The Community Centre’s focus on support services to youth continued to 
develop during the year with the opening of a new Drop-In Centre in Kirkland, 
funded by the municipality and staffed by the YMCA. A three-year project 
involving the YMCA, a CLSC and three high schools was developed to deliver a 
conflict resolution program for youth. 


The YMCA and the West Island Association for the Intellectually Handicapped 
continued to collaborate to provide opportunities for people of all ages who 
have special needs. Two hundred and eighty individuals took part in 
programs designed for people with an intellectual handicap and another 48 
people, with a variety of disabilities, were provided the support needed to 
integrate into regular community activities. 


Du Parc YMCA 


The Du Parc centre inaugurated the cooperative ‘ Jeunesse de Service’ in 
which 15 young people between the ages of 15 to 17 created their own summer 
employment opportunities, thus developing their entrepreneurial skills. 


In partnership with the Montreal Urban Community Police Department, the 
YMCA launched a program called ‘Jeunes a Coeur’. Over 20 at risk young 
people between the ages of 11 and 15 from different cultural backgrounds 
participate in the program. Each youth is paired with a police officer and 
together they engage in educational, sporting, recreational and social 
activities. The center received recognition from the Police Department for its 
role in offering a variety of crime prevention programs in the community. 


Guy Favreau YMCA 


In partnership with the CLSC des Faubourgs and Chinese Family Services, the 
YMCA conducted prenatal aquaform classes and a number of other programs 
for young people from the Chinese community. 


Members at the center once again demonstrated their concern for others by 
contributing almost 500 stuffed animals for distribution to abused children. 


Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA 


A team from the YMCA participated for the second year in the Sport Challenge 
for handicapped persons. In collaboration with Le Centre des Jeunes Boyce- 
Vision and in conjunction with Operation Espoir, young people from the YMCA 
painted a symbolic mural in a neighbourhood housing project. 


In collaboration with the Olympic Installations Board and the Fédération des 
grandes tours, the YMCA organized the first annual Tower Run at the Olympic 
Stadium. Isabelle Ledroit, who won the ladies competition went on to win the 
World Tower Run championship held in Vienna, Austria. 


Kamp Kanawana 


Kamp Kanawana’s year was one full of tradition and innovation. This was 
the first time that programs were offered to groups other than summer 
campers. A group of 50 Korean students between the ages of 11 and 15 
participated in traditional camp activities for four days, sleeping in tents, 
cooking on open fires and integrating with the campers. 


The occupancy rate during the Summer of 96 was 92%. In addition to campers 
from Quebec and several other Provinces, campers came from as far afield as 
the Arctic, Iceland, England, France, Germany, Spain, Russia, Hungary, Korea 
and the USA. 


Notre-Dame-de-Grace YMCA 


The highlight this past year was the major renovation which was completed. 
Over $300,000 was invested to upgrade facilities and equipment. This 
included the construction of a new conditioning room, renovations to locker 
rooms and the service desk area, refurbishing the gym and painting the 
entire building. 


Child development as well as aquatics continued to grow and the teen 
program welcomed its 400th participant after less than one year of operation. 
The number of members reached 1,700. 


Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA 


Work continued with community groups and municipal officials to find ways 
to better utilize the facility on Ash Street. Fitness facilities were closed in 
September 95. The activities of the Branch were focused on community 
development work and programs for youth. 


Saint-Laurent YMCA 


At long last, the YMCA was issued a license to operate a daycare for 55 
children. There is a second independent daycare which operates at the center 
and it has a license for 85 children. In addition, the YMCA is licensed to 
provide child care in the home and 125 children are involved in this program. 


The conditioning facilities were expanded and new equipment was added. 
These improvements plus some added parking contributed to an increase in 
the number of members and in member satisfaction. 


Westmount YMCA 


This was one of the most successful years at the center. The number of 
members increased and member satisfaction improved thanks, in part, to the 
investment in new equipment and the measures taken to meet the Priority 
SAM standards of excellence. 


Child Development programs were fully subscribed. The YMCA, in partnership 
with the City of Westmount, operated a Teen Center which provides various 
programs developed and managed by teens in the community. 


The St. Valentines Casino was a great success. Over 250 people attended and 
the proceeds were used to purchase a hydraulic lift for the pool, thus giving 
accessibility to persons with disabilities. 


West Island YMCA 


Facility improvements and new equipment at the Brunswick Family Centre 
had a significant positive impact on members, staff and volunteers. New 
initiatives and programs were introduced such as stroller aerobics and 
triathlon training. 


In partnership with the Town of Baie D’Urfe, the YMCA started a pre-school 
day camp and opened a youth drop-in center in the community. 


Over 15 community organizations were given access to the Brunswick facility 
throughout the year and 385 individuals and/or families were provided with 
financial subsidies to enable them to participate in membership and program 
activities.

Message from the Chairman of the Board and the 
President of the Montreal YMCA Foundation 


Revenues for the year ended May 31, 1996 were $310,567 compared to 
$434,301 the previous year. Donations to the Montreal YMCA and the expenses 
of the Foundation were adjusted to reflect the decrease in revenues with the 
result that the surplus in fiscal 96 was the equal of that in fiscal 95. 


The decline in contributions is disappointing. It reflects, in part, the growing 
demands that are made on individuals and companies to fund the ever 
increasing needs of the less advantaged in our society. It also points out the 
necessity for the Montreal YMCA to better inform the community with respect 
to the value and relevance of its programs and activities. It can no longer 
afford to be one of the best kept secrets in town! 


The Foundation mandated a firm to research the community’s receptivity to a 
capital campaign, the purpose of which would be to construct a new 
downtown YMCA to replace the existing structure on Drummond Street which 
was built in 1912. While the results of.the survey are encouraging, it is 
obvious that the YMCA will not be able to finance the entire cost of the project. 
The YMCA is in discussion with the City of Montreal and Concordia University 
to determine if a joint project is feasible. If so, the Foundation would be 
expected to launch a capital campaign early in 1997. 


Thanks to the efforts of the staff and the generosity of sponsors, the Special 
Events including the Heritage Club Dinner, the Benefit Evening with Le Cirque 
du Soleil and the Golf Tournament were all outstanding successes. We extend 
our appreciation to our fellow Directors who assisted with the organization, 
provided the financing and supported these worthwhile events. 


We note with deep regret the passing of Maurice Masse. Maurice gave 
decades of volunteer service to the Montreal YMCA and was one of the 
founding directors of the Foundation. Maurice was awarded the Fellowship of 
Honour which is the highest form of recognition granted a volunteer by the 
YMCA movement. 


Fewer than fifty individuals have been so honoured in Canada. Maurice 
taught us compassion, perseverance and enthusiasm. His passing marks the 
end of an era and he will be sorely missed. Our thoughts are with his son 
Bernard and all who loved and admired this remarkable man. 


The Gabrielle and Maurice Masse Award 


The Heritage Club, which comprises over one hundred members, held its 13th 
annual banquet on April 22,1996. This event is an opportunity for the 
Montreal YMCA to pay tribute to those individuals who have made an 
important contribution to the development of the Association. 


The honouree and recipient of the Gabrielle and Maurice Masse Award this 
year was John E. Cleghorn in recognition of the leadership he provided as 
Chairman of the Montreal YMCA during a particularly tumultuous time in its 
history and the important role he played during the Foundation’s last capital 
campaign. Through his unwavering loyalty and tireless efforts, John 
Cleghorn made a significant contribution to the mission and development of 
the Montreal YMCA. 


John’s early experience with the YMCA was first as a camper and later as 
counselor at Kamp Kanawana. Several Kanawana alumni were present at the 
banquet and the years have not hindered the lively spirit of the former 
campers and staff. 


The memorable evening was organized by William Ridley and Suzanne 
Aboud, both former recipients of the Gabrielle and Maurice Masse Award. Our 
thanks to the four Heritage Club members who anonymously sponsored the 
event. 


Investments, Endowment and Planned Giving 


Endowment and Planned Giving, initiated in November 1988, encompass the 
following: endowment, insurance, inheritance, gifts of art, marketable 
securities and real estate. The value of the endowment fund as at May 31, 
1996 was $1,942,577. Income from the endowment fund totaled $153,549 of 
which $115,700 of designated and non-designated funds were contributed to 
the Montreal YMCA. 


Annual Campaign 


In the year ended May 31, 1996 the annual campaign raised $108,787. This 
represents only part of the money that was raised during the campaign. 
Those contributions received subsequent to May 31st are accounted for in the 
present fiscal year. These funds are used to finance subsidies for those 
persons who cannot pay the full price of a membership or a program fee and 
to help fund international development programs. The success of the annual 
campaign depends on the efforts of hundreds of volunteers and staff as well 
as the generosity of the contributors. 


Benefit Evening 


Recognized for its humanitarian deeds and its work with youth, the Montreal 
YMCA was selected by the Cirque du Soleil among a number of worthy 
organizations as the beneficiary of a Benefit Evening performance. Held at 
the Old Port on the evening of May 9th, over 800 people attended thereby 
contributing $62,664 which was used to finance YMCA programs and activities 
designed to meet the needs of our youth. We gratefully acknowledge the 
financial support of our sponsors without whom this evening would not have 
been possible: Imasco Limited, Tele-Direct (Publications) Inc., and Pratt & 
Whitney Canada Inc. 


Golf Tournament 


The 11th edition of the Foundation’s golf tournament was held on June 3, 1996 
at the magnificent Pinegrove Golf and Country Club. This event, in which 160 
golfers participated, raised $42,844 which was used to finance YMCA youth 
programs. Our thanks to the Tournament Patrons for their generosity: Royal 
Bank of Canada, Bell Canada, Ciment Saint-Laurent, Fédération des caisses 
populaires Desjardins de Montreal et de I’Ouest-du-Quebec, Celanese Canada 
Inc., Lafleur Brown, Langlois Robert, Merck Frosst Canada Inc. and Montrusco 
and Associates Inc. 


Our thanks also to the 29 sponsors and to the 35 companies or individuals who 
graciously donated prizes and to the members of the Organizing Committee 
for their dedication and effort namely, Charles S. Lafontaine, Serge A. 
Jacques and Richard Dufresne. 


Vd ay 


John D. Thompson Marcel Coté 
Chairman of the Board President
